purpose: De-identified program-level event ledger for the FTC Amazon Flex tip-refund administration; it separates formal compensation, distribution, reissue, individual receipt, and downstream worker power.

events.geography: United States; FTC Amazon Flex driver tip-refund program
events.date_precision: program administration status as of 31 Dec 2024; underlying practice late 2016 through Aug 2019 and payment rounds span 2021–2026
events.denominator: Named refund program and eligible Amazon Flex drivers; complete eligible-driver denominator and driver-level status file are not public
events.method: Structured extraction from FTC consent-order announcement, official payment announcements, current refund-administration page, annual refund report, and retained canonical observation record
events.missingness: The public program record does not disclose driver-level eligibility, amount due, individual receipt timing, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household recovery, bargaining position, trust, or exit; aggregate counts are not individual outcomes
events.exposure: FTC alleged that Amazon withheld customer tips from Flex drivers between late 2016 and August 2019
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative platforms, other work, non-use, savings, and household support are not observed; payment-channel friction is visible only through the uncashed-check reissue route
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Potential withheld-tip income is the reported worker burden; individual tip amounts, timing, and net household incidence are not observed
events.choice_or_response: FTC enforcement produced a consent order, payment rounds, and a current Zelle reissue route for eligible drivers who did not cash earlier checks
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Amazon controlled the underlying pay practice and payment administration; the FTC controlled enforcement and public refund reporting
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The consent order designated $61,710,583 for driver compensation; FTC reports more than $60.6 million distributed through earlier rounds, 2,806 successful Zelle reissue payments, and 130,952 drivers reported fully compensated as of the annual report cutoff
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate administrator-reported distribution and successful reissue counts; driver-level receipt is not retained
events.durability_followup: Continued work, alternative work, bargaining power, trust, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Program-level payment distribution and reissue stages are observed; individual receipt, amount received, and remaining loss are not
events.protected_outcome: Aggregate payment reach is reported, but no driver-level protected income, restored work opportunity, or household security is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: The alleged withheld-tip income and possible payment-channel friction are visible as program risks; residual loss, unpaid time, and household trade-offs remain unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The formal order and administrator distribution move a compensation obligation toward eligible drivers, while eligibility, delivery, cashing, and residual risk remain distributed across the program and workers
events.later_outcome: Aggregate participation rose from 90.3% to 92.3% after the Zelle route in the reported program measure; continued platform work, alternative work, bargaining, household recovery, trust, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The enforcement record attributes the practice and remedy architecture but supplies no worker-reported fairness, dignity, trust, or dependence measure
events.public_or_collective_response: FTC enforcement and public refund administration are observed; driver organizing, bargaining, political action, and individual complaint effort are not
events.counterexample: Administrator-reported distribution can advance payment reach without proving every driver received the amount due or changed platform use; failure to cash an earlier check can reflect channel or address friction rather than refusal
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official FTC consent-order, payment-distribution, 2024 annual-refund report, and current refund-administration records; the 2024 report states 2,806 successful Zelle payments, 92.3% reported participation, and 130,952 drivers fully compensated for more than $58.5 million as of 31 Dec 2024, but aggregate program measures are not representative worker estimates and do not prove any one driver's amount, timing, residual loss, or recovery

arrows.evidence: FTC consent-order announcement identifies the late-2016-to-August-2019 practice and a $61,710,583 driver-compensation obligation
arrows.counterexample: A formal amount does not identify each driver's exposure, amount due, or net loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Driver-level exposure, tip amount, eligibility, and contemporaneous notice

arrows.evidence: FTC reports November 2021 and May 2025 distribution rounds totaling more than $60.6 million
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate dollars and rounds are not a payment rate or average driver recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Complete eligible denominator, amount due, payment status, and failed-delivery categories

arrows.from: uncashed or unaccepted first payment channel
arrows.evidence: FTC reports a current Zelle route for eligible drivers who did not cash checks and 2,806 successful Zelle payments in the annual report
arrows.counterexample: A reissue route is evidence of administrative follow-up, not proof that the reissued payment reached or was usable by each driver
arrows.remaining_gap: Driver-level reissue eligibility, payment date/channel, cashing, fees, and failure reason

arrows.evidence: The program reports 130,952 drivers fully compensated and participation rising from 90.3% to 92.3%, but publishes no driver-level linkage or residual-loss file
arrows.counterexample: Program-level reach can coexist with unknown individual receipt, amount, timing, and remaining loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Identifier-bearing eligible-driver ledger, receipt, amount, timing, remaining loss, and correction

arrows.to: continued work, alternatives, bargaining, or exit
arrows.evidence: Public refund records contain no driver-level follow-up on continued Flex work, alternative work, household security, bargaining, trust, or exit
arrows.counterexample: Receipt may coexist with continued platform use, switching, or no observed behavioral change; none can be inferred from distribution
arrows.remaining_gap: Post-payment work and alternative route, household outcome, worker voice, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger advances the evidence from compensation obligation to administrator-reported distribution and reissue. It does not establish individual payment receipt, full recovery, restored opportunity, continued or alternative work, bargaining power, household security, trust, or exit.
storage_boundary: No driver file, payment roster, or bulk personal data is retained; only official aggregate program measures, source metadata, and explicit missingness boundaries are represented.
